newsitem.title: USA: ConEd N.Y. nuke seen back on line this week.
newsitem.headline: ConEd N.Y. nuke seen back on line this week.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc's (ConEd) 975 megawatt Indian Point nuclear power unit 2 should resume power production this week following a repair outage, a company spokeswoman said Monday.
The unit, at Indian Point, N.Y., has been moved to a hot shutdown mode from cold shutdown in preparation for a resumption of electricity production, said spokeswoman Joan Burger.
Indian Point 2 was shut Jan 27 to repair a feedwater valve.

ConEd representatives met with Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) officials last week to address NRC concerns over debris that had been found in the unit's feedwater and condensate systems, Burger said.
The debris was blamed for the valve problem.

Separately, the adjacent Indian Point nuclear power unit 3 was operating at full power as of Monday morning following a shutdown Jan 18 to repair feedwater heaters, the NRC said in a plant status report Monday.
The 965 MW Indian Point 3, operated by the New York Power Authority, returned to full power over the weekend.
